description:
Londoners can now travel in autonomous cars for the first time, after Uber was granted a licence to operate a test fleet of self-driving vehicles. Each vehicle must have a safety driver behind the wheel, but the UK government says fully self-driving cars will be available in late 2027.

Driverless cars are the latest threat facing London’s iconic black cabs, over a decade after the introduction of ride-sharing apps revolutionised transport in the city.
Tristan Redman meets Tom Scullion, who has been a cabbie for over 30 years, and asks whether one of the world’s hardest memory tests – the Knowledge – can compete with AI.

With just days to go until the midterm elections, the Democrats believe they could flip as many as six seats in the Senate. What are the polls telling us with just days to go until the midterm elections, and could results still go in Donald Trump's favour?   

The Democrats have been trying to oust Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins for almost three decades. With the midterms days away, President Donald Trump’s unpopularity could see her finally removed. The Maine election has become a referendum on how voters view Senator Collins. Mainers are deciding if they continue to trust the woman who has climbed the ranks of the Republican party and brought millions of dollars of federal money to their state, or if they find her affiliation with Trump too much. Her contender, progressive Democrat Troy Jackson is a late entrant to the race, after his predecessor Graham Platner suspended his campaign following a series of scandals that included a woman accusing him of sexual assault. author: BBC News
description:
Up to 750 Ukrainians living in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been given the opportunity to evacuate as part of a temporary local ceasefire - brokered with the help of Pope Leo and US First Lady Melania Trump. 

The evacuation was overseen by the Ukrainian and Russian human rights ombudsmen. But our correspondent in Kyiv tells us that some evacuees are nervous about the journey, which will take them deeper into Russian-controlled territory and into Belarus before they can re-enter Ukraine. Analysts have also said Vladimir Putin may be using this operation as a propaganda tool. 

We speak to a journalist just across the river from Oleshky, in Kherson, about the dire humanitarian conditions there. And we ask our Ukraine analyst how this ceasefire fits into the wider picture of the war.

author: BBC News
description:
An Australian athlete has admitted putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event.
 
Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that".
 
Challenged over why she carried on, she said: “I didn’t really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I’m truly sorry for everyone that I did affect.”
 
The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was “traumatic”. She also said she considered walking away from the sport.

Although initially appearing defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race.

title: Hyrox athlete who soiled herself admits putting others ‘at risk’ but backlash ‘traumatic’ | BBC News
